primary_web_sources.scope: Current subscription collection versus sending eligibility, worker/button contracts
HTTPS, origin, MIME, default scope and existing registration

contracts: Any-plan collection requires a configured active channel, origin/channel resolution; sending eligibility is separate. New custom channel UI itself is quota-gated, so retain support setup prerequisite rather than promising any-plan creation.
Public Business ID, never private API token; SDK public configuration provides VAPID key.
initialize resolves before worker readiness; subscribe requests permission in click before await and waits registration/activation; readiness wait has bounded timeout.
Workers must preserve existing handlers, same origin and scope; foreign application key is rejected.
Subscription browser ownership versus server Response.succeeded; failure can leave browser subscription for background sync.
Unsubscribe null versus succeeded/failed/undefined; disable identity first, remove browser subscription second; no removal when server response fails.
Current page false does not revoke permission/unsubscribe other devices; subscribed is local truthiness, not latest server acknowledgement.
Current Rails worker supports data.actions[event.action] fallback data.url; source guard, skipWaiting, generic-handler ordering retained.
